title: Phase 5 spatial-analysis contracts
description: One entry per table written by `python -m src.analysis.build`, in the same dialect as bronze/silver/gold. Row shape in `properties`; grain, row-count floor and cross-column invariants in `x-table-constraints`. These tables differ from gold's in what can go wrong with them: the types are all numbers and the columns are all derived, so a type check catches almost nothing, and the real defects are relational -- a `significant` flag that disagrees with the p-value that produced it, a class label that disagrees with the sign of its own z-score, a per-capita rate on a cell whose population was refused. That is what `row_rules` is for, and every rule here corresponds to a way one of these tables could be published looking entirely plausible and being wrong.

analysis.cell_stats_h3_r8.title: Per-cell crash statistics over the filled study area
analysis.cell_stats_h3_r8.description: One row per H3 r8 cell overlapping the study-area county polygon, INCLUDING cells with zero crashes: a hot-spot test run only over cells that had a crash conditions on the outcome and can neither find a cold spot nor see the zero that makes its neighbour hot. `population` is ACS 2023 5-year B01003_001E area-apportioned from block groups in EPSG:5070 (equal-area, because the apportionment is a ratio of areas); it is a DENOMINATOR and never a per-record feature. `rate_is_defined` is false where population is under [analysis] min_population_for_rate, and `rate_per_1k_pop` is null there rather than infinite -- those cells (interchanges, the airport, parkland) stay in the raw-count analysis, which is the entire point of the raw-versus-normalised contrast.

row_rules.name: injury_within_crashes
row_rules.description: severity counts nest: fatal <= injury <= crashes (KABCO K is an injury)

row_rules.name: rate_defined_iff_population
row_rules.description: rate_is_defined must equal population >= [analysis] min_population_for_rate. The literal 50 is duplicated from config/geo.toml on purpose -- a contract is a fixed assertion and cannot read a config file -- and tests/test_analysis.py asserts the two agree, so lowering the floor in config without restating it here fails a test rather than quietly making this rule vacuous.

row_rules.name: rate_null_when_undefined
row_rules.description: a cell with no usable denominator carries NULL, never inf and never a rate over three people

row_rules.name: rate_present_when_defined
row_rules.predicate: NOT rate_is_defined OR rate_per_1k_pop IS NOT NULL
row_rules.description: a cell with a usable denominator must actually carry its rate

row_rules.name: rate_finite
row_rules.description: no inf/NaN survives into a published rate

row_rules.name: rate_per_km2_iff_land
row_rules.description: a density over land exists exactly where there is land

row_rules.name: period_ordered
row_rules.description: the study period is a period

analysis.lisa_h3_r8.title: Local Moran's I (LISA) per cell and variable
analysis.lisa_h3_r8.description: esda.Moran_Local with 999 conditional permutations and a fixed seed, on row-standardised k=1 hex contiguity weights. `p_fdr` is the Benjamini-Hochberg threshold (esda.fdr) for the whole variable's p-value vector -- a single number repeated on every row of that variable, not a per-row adjusted p -- and `significant` is `p_sim <= p_fdr`. `quadrant_uncorrected` is the same classification at the uncorrected alpha, kept as a column so the correction's effect is a measurement rather than a sentence. HH/LL are clusters; LH/HL are spatial outliers and are usually a single intersection.

row_rules.name: significant_matches_threshold
row_rules.description: the significance flag is the FDR test, not a second opinion about it

row_rules.name: quadrant_ns_iff_not_significant
row_rules.description: a quadrant is only classified where the corrected test passes

row_rules.name: fdr_no_looser_than_alpha
row_rules.description: a correction that raised the threshold above alpha would be a correction in the wrong direction

row_rules.name: corrected_set_within_uncorrected
row_rules.description: FDR can only remove cells from the significant set, never add one

analysis.gi_star_h3_r8.title: Getis-Ord Gi* per cell and variable
analysis.gi_star_h3_r8.description: esda.G_Local(star=True) with 999 permutations and a fixed seed, on BINARY k=1 hex contiguity weights -- binary because Gi* compares a neighbourhood SUM to the global sum, and row-standardising would turn it into a comparison of means and stop it being an intensity test. `star=True` puts the cell in its own neighbourhood, which is what lets a single intense cell register. `hotspot_class` is the FDR-corrected classification, `hotspot_class_uncorrected` the same classification at raw alpha; `p_bonferroni` is reported for comparison and is deliberately not what the class column uses.

row_rules.name: significant_matches_threshold
row_rules.description: the significance flag is the FDR test result

row_rules.name: class_ns_iff_not_significant
row_rules.description: a cell is classified hot or cold exactly where the corrected test passes

row_rules.name: class_sign_matches_z
row_rules.description: HOT requires a positive z and COLD a negative one -- the label must agree with the statistic that produced it

row_rules.name: corrected_set_within_uncorrected
row_rules.description: the FDR-significant set is a subset of the uncorrected one

row_rules.name: fdr_no_looser_than_alpha
row_rules.description: the corrected threshold never exceeds alpha

analysis.hotspot_contrast.title: Cells whose Gi* class changes under population normalisation
analysis.hotspot_contrast.description: The assignment's explicit ask -- 'show that population normalization changes the answer' -- as a table rather than a paragraph. One row per cell whose FDR-corrected Gi* class differs between raw counts and the per-capita rate. `contrast_kind` HOT_RAW_ONLY is volume without risk (a busy cell that is busy because that is where the people are); HOT_RATE_ONLY is risk without volume, which is what a raw-count map hides; RATE_UNDEFINED is a cell the normalised analysis could not score at all because its population is below the floor, reported rather than dropped because that is itself the finding. `place_name` is the modal snapped OSM road name in the cell: a label so the prose can name the place, not a claim that the road caused anything.

row_rules.name: classes_actually_differ
row_rules.description: every row of a contrast table is a cell whose class changed; a row where they agree does not belong here

row_rules.name: undefined_kind_matches_class
row_rules.description: the kind and the class must tell the same story about a missing denominator

row_rules.name: undefined_has_no_rate
row_rules.description: a cell the normalised analysis refused cannot carry a rate

analysis.kde_surface.title: Kernel density surfaces at every reported bandwidth
analysis.kde_surface.description: A regular grid in EPSG:26985 (NAD83 / Maryland, metres) -- named on every row rather than assumed, because a grid of bare (x, y) doubles with no frame is not a spatial output. One block of rows per bandwidth so the three surfaces can be compared on an identical grid and colour scale. `density` is a probability density per square metre and integrates to ~1 over the grid (the build asserts it, which checks the grid extent and the area units at once); `intensity_per_km2` is that times N times 1e6, i.e. expected crashes per square kilometre over the study period, which is the number an operations reader can act on. `bandwidth_method` records how each bandwidth was arrived at: cross-validated on spatially blocked folds, a Gaussian rule of thumb, or the off-the-shelf practitioner control.

row_rules.name: projected_crs_only
row_rules.description: EPSG:3857 is for tiles. A bandwidth measured in Web Mercator at 39.1N is wrong by 1/cos(lat) ~ 1.29

row_rules.name: density_finite
row_rules.description: no inf/NaN in a published surface

analysis.crash_year_counts.title: Crashes per calendar year in the study corpus
analysis.crash_year_counts.description: The data behind the first figure, and the evidence for the period choice: a per-year table is what shows the 2020 pandemic drop and the partial final year that would otherwise be read as a spatial finding. Figures are not required to be byte-identical between runs (matplotlib embeds versions); the table behind each one is.

row_rules.name: injury_within_crashes
row_rules.description: severity counts nest

analysis.st_clusters.title: ST-DBSCAN clusters, tight in space and in time
analysis.st_clusters.description: Clusters found with two independent thresholds -- [analysis.st_dbscan] eps_space_m in EPSG:26985 metres and eps_time_h in hours -- so a cluster is a set of crashes that are near each other AND close in time, which is the recurring-corridor result the assignment asks for rather than the year-long smear a space-only epsilon produces. sklearn's DBSCAN takes one metric, so the neighbourhood is built directly as a sparse 0/1 matrix that is true only where both conditions hold. `span_days` is the discriminator: the same run with the time condition removed is reported beside this one, and its clusters span the whole study period.

row_rules.name: projected_crs_only
row_rules.description: the spatial epsilon is metres in a projected CRS, never Web Mercator

row_rules.name: injury_within_crashes
row_rules.description: severity counts nest

row_rules.name: dates_ordered
row_rules.predicate: first_crash_date IS NULL OR last_crash_date IS NULL OR first_crash_date <= last_crash_date
row_rules.description: a cluster's first crash precedes its last
